brief: A file organizer as a spatial canvas — documents arranged by topic proximity, not lists or grids

dominant_strengths: Subtle colored glows on each cluster create gentle topic differentiation without overwhelming the dark canvas surface
Consistent card anatomy (title, timestamp, owner, status dot) makes scanning predictable across heterogeneous clusters
Spatial grouping reads as semantic proximity, supporting the brief better than a flat list or grid would
dominant_weaknesses: Connecting lines between clusters are barely visible and inconsistent — spatial relationships feel implied rather than authored
Cluster placement is essentially a loose grid masquerading as canvas; no zoom, no minimap, no true spatial affordance shown
Floating color swatch palette and Focus/Organize/New chips feel like orphaned UI fragments without clear hierarchy or purpose
fix_priorities: Strengthen inter-cluster edges or use gradient fields to make topical proximity readable as a system, not decoration
Add canvas affordances (zoom level, pan cursor, minimap) so the spatial metaphor is behaviorally true, not just visual
Resolve the floating swatch grid bottom-right — either integrate as legend/tag picker or remove
Tighten typographic hierarchy: titles, metadata, and owner labels currently share too-similar weight and contrast
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral glow and dark-canvas mood lead, but behavioral canvas mechanics are underdeveloped and reflective payoff is modest.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially — clusters suggest topic proximity, but without true canvas interaction or meaningful edges it still reads closer to grouped panels than a spatial workspace.
